note: Q-set (scenarios S2/S7): 12 questions = 4 paraphrases, 2 multi-hop, 2 exception/scope, 2 unknown/conflict, 2 current-vs-target. expected.status is one of ANSWERED, ABSTAINED, NEEDS_CLARIFICATION, PARTIAL. must_cite entries are evidence_ref strings from expected_knowledge.json; must_not lists claims that make the answer wrong. Expectations are fixed before any tuning and must not be changed to match model output. Questions tagged after_target_accepted are asked against the accepted target of scenario S7. Exception (versioned, history kept): an expectation may change only after a recorded business decision by the owner; the old expectation and the runs that failed against it stay in `expected_history`, and a changed item is no longer unseen. Fixture version 2 (2026-10-17): Q10 after the owner's decision (option B) - an oracle correction, not a model improvement. A versioned item may give `status_any_of` instead of `status`.

questions.text: Who has to sign off a 1.2 million yen purchase?
Does a 900,000 JPY purchase need a person to approve it?
Whose approval does a purchase from a risky supplier need, whatever the price?
At what amount does a standard request stop being approved automatically?
A CAPEX request for a supplier on the risk register is 3,000,000 JPY. Who ends up with it and why?

expected.must_note: the CAPEX Finance threshold is disputed (2,000,000 vs 5,000,000) so the Finance leg must be flagged, not decided

questions.text: Which roles can be involved in approving a request, and which rules put them there?
Is there an exception for emergency purchases?

expected.must_note: the guide says fast-tracked automatically but emergency.py still routes 1,000,000 JPY and above to a manager and CAPEX 2,000,000 JPY and above to Finance

questions.text: Does the Finance rule for CAPEX apply to emergency purchases too?

expected.must_note: code applies it, the policy text is silent about emergencies

questions.text: From which CAPEX amount does Finance review a request?

expected.must_note: both values must be shown as conflicting; no winner is chosen without a human decision

questions.text: Who approves a purchase of a type the policy does not mention, like a software subscription of 4 million yen?

expected.status_note: PARTIAL when the part the evidence supports is answered; NEEDS_CLARIFICATION when a classification must be confirmed before continuing. No single status is forced for every wording.
expected.must_note: If the transaction is a purchase request within the policy's scope, 4,000,000 JPY meets the 1,000,000 JPY manager-approval threshold (policy 2.1, manager guide, approval.yaml, routing.py agree). Finance is not concluded without evidence that it is CAPEX; if it is CAPEX the sources disagree (config/code 2,000,000 -> Finance; policy/guide 5,000,000 -> Finance Controller) and the conflict is kept, not resolved. 'Reviewed by IT governance' is not 'approved by IT governance'. The licence-renewal rule is not applied to a new subscription unless the evidence confirms it is a renewal. The answer names what is still missing.
missing_facts: whether it is a purchase request within the procurement policy's scope
new subscription or renewal of an existing licence
supplier.risk (high-risk register -> Operations Director regardless of amount)

oracle_change.kind: oracle correction after a business decision (owner, option B)
oracle_change.source_check: procurement-policy.md 2.1 (type-agnostic: purchase requests of JPY 1,000,000 or more need the department manager), manager-guide.md (one million yen or more), approval.yaml standard_manager_threshold_jpy 1000000, routing.py (CAPEX>=2M -> Finance before the manager threshold; high-risk supplier first). CAPEX threshold conflict 2,000,000 vs 5,000,000 kept (expected_gaps capex-threshold-conflict). rule-license-renewal is a retrieval distractor from another document (doc-other), outcome quarterly_review, not part of the Harbor source scope.
